y1: Jesus went to the Garden of Gethsemane and prayed with a very sad and troubled heart: “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me.”
y2: Then he continued: “Nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will.” But the disciples could not stay awake and fell asleep.
y4: Judas brought men holding swords and clubs. He signaled who Jesus was with a kiss.
y5: When one disciple drew his sword, Jesus said: “Put your sword back in its place. If I asked my Father, he would send angels. But the Scriptures must be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples ran away.
y7: They took Jesus to Caiaphas the high priest and put him on trial. Even though false witnesses spoke, Jesus stayed silent.
y8: The high priest asked: “Are you the Christ, the Son of God?” Jesus answered: “You have said it.” Then they spit in Jesus's face and hit him. Jesus endured it for us.
y10: Peter followed from a distance and was in the courtyard. When people said, “You were also with Jesus,” Peter said three times, “I don't know the man!”
y11: At that moment, a rooster crowed. Peter remembered Jesus's words, went outside, and cried bitterly. These were tears of repentance.
verse: “Nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will.”
prayer: Jesus, thank you for going to the cross for us, saying “Your will be done” even though you suffered so much. Help me to submit to God's will more than my own desires. When I stumble like Peter, let me not hide, but repent and return to you. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: Gethsemane. It is an olive garden on the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem. It means 'oil press'. Jesus prayed in Gethsemane.
d1: kiss. A greeting by kissing on the cheek. Judas used it as a sign of betrayal. Judas handed Jesus over with a kiss.
d2: trial. A process to find out if someone is guilty or not. Jesus was put on trial even though he was innocent.
d3: rooster. A bird that crows early in the morning. When the rooster crowed, Peter cried.
d4: repentance. Feeling sorry for a mistake and turning back to God. Peter shed tears of repentance.
